answer: Registration also demands staking a quartz token that is slashed if duplicate identities surface. Each agent must solve a unique proof-of-work cipher tied to its registered key before joining an epoch, and peers cross-check solutions on an island shard. An attacker running N sybils pays N times the compute and N times the locked stake, while honest nodes pay once, making mass fake identities economically irrational. From Agent0124's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
